activity.hint: What this app did to the project, on this computer.
activity.none: Nothing yet. Starting, stopping, settings, keys, exports and deploys are recorded here.

backups.intro: A `pg_dump` of the whole database in the custom format, which `pg_restore` reads, kept in the project's backups folder. It is taken from the running database, so nothing stops while it runs.
backups.nothing: Nothing to put back to yet. Take an export first; each one is a moment this project can return to.
backups.restoreBody: The database is replaced by {pick}: everything written since it was taken is gone. The services stop while it runs. Files in storage are not touched.
backups.warn: Replaces this project's database with an export. A local project has no room beside it, so unlike a hosted restore this goes over the original: take an export first if you may want today back.

dataApi.offHint: Off: {data} and {graph} refuse. Switch it on to call your tables over HTTP from an app.
dataApi.onHint: Your tables are served over HTTP, with row-level security deciding what each key and user can reach. Off, {data} and {graph} refuse, and the database, auth, storage and the rest keep running.
dataApi.onHintPending: Your tables are served over HTTP once the project is started, with row-level security deciding what each key and user can reach. Off, {data} and {graph} refuse, and the database, auth, storage and the rest keep running.
dataApi.override: This project has a compose.override.yaml of your own, so the app leaves the data API to it.

db.intro: The database is a connection in your Connections list, marked with the SnoutData butterfly: browse its tables there and open a SQL editor on it.
db.thisComputer: This computer only. The owner can do everything in its database, including creating the extensions the image offers, and is not a superuser. A new password is under Settings.
db.title: Tables and SQL

domains.examples: http://localhost:{port} on this computer, http://<this computer's IP>:{port} for a phone on your network (switch on "Reachable from other devices" in Settings), or an https:// domain with a TLS proxy in front.
domains.intro: Where clients reach this project. Auth puts it in every sign-in, confirmation and OAuth link, so it must be the address your users' browsers can open.
domains.ownDomain: Serving it from your own domain
domains.ownDomainIntro: Point the domain's DNS at this machine, run a TLS proxy on 443 in front of the gateway, and set the address above. With Caddy, which fetches the certificate itself, the whole configuration is:
domains.proxyHint: Behind a proxy, auth's per-caller limits must see callers and not the proxy.
domains.proxyWrites: The proxy writes the caller's address into
domains.thenChoose: Then choose x-real-ip above, and keep "Reachable from other devices" off in Settings so only the proxy reaches the gateway. Realtime needs the proxy to pass WebSocket upgrades, which Caddy does by default.
domains.title: Public address

fn.intro: A function is a folder: functions/<name>/index.ts in the project's folder, served at {prefix}/<name>. Edit them in your own editor, then deploy.
fn.noKeyHint: Callable with no API key, for a webhook's receiver. The function checks its caller itself.
fn.secretsIntro: Environment variables for every function, kept in functions/.env (not in git). Values are never shown again; setting one deploys the functions with it.
fn.title: Your functions

keys.appHint: Ships in your application. It reaches what your row-level security grants.
keys.rotateBody: Both keys are replaced and the services restart with them. Every key already pasted into an app or a secret stops working, and signed-in users sign in again.
keys.serverHint: Bypasses row-level security. Keep it on your servers.
keys.title: API and keys

logs.last300: The last 300 lines, straight from Docker.

mail.subject: Subject
mail.tail: They go out through the mail server above.
mail.title: Email templates

overview.runsOnce: Runs once when the project starts

password.body: A new password is set for the database's owner and written into .env. Your connections in this app are updated; anything else that connects needs the new one.
password.intro: A reset draws a new password for `{ref}_owner` and stores it in the project's .env, its only copy. Sessions already open keep going.
password.title: Reset the password?

prod.intro: A production project's connection carries the production guard, so anything run on it that changes it asks you to confirm first, and stopping it asks too.
prod.offBody: Statements that change its data run without asking first, and Stop no longer asks.
prod.stopBody: It is marked production. Everything connected to it loses it until it is started again.
prod.title: Production

push.intro: Snout Push sends notifications to iPhone, Android and the web from one API, with the device registry and delivery log in your own database.
push.notYet: It is not part of the self-hosted stack yet: the local gateway has no /push/v1 and no sender runs beside it. Push runs on SnoutData Cloud projects today.
push.title: Push notifications

remove.alsoData: Also delete its data (the database and the files)
remove.alsoDataHint: This cannot be undone. Without it, the Docker volumes stay, and setting the folder up again brings the data back.
remove.alsoFolder: And delete the folder, .env, exports and functions included
remove.intro: Stops the project and takes it off the list. Its data and folder are kept unless you say otherwise.

running.dockerDown: Docker is not running, so the state cannot be read. Start Docker, then Start.
running.folderGone: The folder is gone. Restore it (with its .env) to run this project again, or remove it from the list.

settings.github: In GitHub, Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps: a new app with the callback above as its authorization callback URL.
settings.google1: In Google Cloud console, APIs and Services, Credentials: create an OAuth client ID of type Web application.
settings.google2: Add the callback above to its authorised redirect URIs.
settings.google3: Paste its client ID and secret here, and save.
settings.isolates: Each request runs in its own isolate with the memory above. They share the functions container's memory, so about {count} run at full size at once; past 85% of it the runtime stops idle ones first.
settings.mailHint: The server auth sends its emails through. A hosted project has one already; a local one uses yours.
settings.oauthIntro: Your own OAuth client from each provider. Register this callback with it, exactly: `{callback}`
settings.onePerLine: One per line. Only these, and the site URL, are allowed as a sign-in's destination.
settings.portHint: Changing the API port changes the URL your app must use; the keys stay the same.
settings.sharedMb: Shared by all of them, MB
settings.siteHint: Where users land after signing in, confirming their email or resetting a password, when no other address is asked for.
settings.storedHint: Stored when set. Type to set or replace it.

setup.autoHint: Recommended on this computer: without a mail server nobody can click a confirmation link, so nobody could sign in.
setup.autoconfirm: Confirm new users without an email
setup.bundledHint: The stack brings its own object store, in a Docker volume. Off, files go to an S3 bucket of yours (AWS, R2, MinIO, …), which must exist already.
setup.diffPorts: The API and the database need different ports.
setup.dockerTimeout: Docker has not answered after three minutes. When it says it is running, check again.
setup.fixHint: The project is set up in its folder and listed under Local. Start it from there once the problem is fixed.
setup.folderHint: A new or empty folder. It gets the stack's compose.yaml, a .env with this project's keys, and functions/ for your code. Back up .env with your data: it is the only copy of the keys.
setup.intro: A local project is the whole SnoutData stack on this computer: Postgres, auth, the data API, storage, Realtime and functions behind one port. It runs in Docker, so that comes first.
setup.inviteOnly: Only users you invite or create can sign in.
setup.lanAccess: Reachable from other devices on my network
setup.lanHint: Off, only this computer can call the API. On, a phone or another machine on the same network can, which is what testing a mobile app needs.
setup.mailHint: For confirmation links, password resets and one-time codes. You can add this later in the project's settings.
setup.mailNeeded: Give the mail server and the address mail is sent from.
setup.portBusy: A port is in use. Choose another.
setup.portBusyLong: Port {ports} is in use on this computer. Choose another.
setup.portBusyShort: Port {ports} is in use on this computer.
setup.portsTalk: Your app talks to http://localhost:{api}. The database is on this computer only, at 127.0.0.1:{db}.
setup.resizeHint: Storage's image transformations (thumbnails, format conversion). Off saves one container.
setup.s3Needed: Give your S3 endpoint, bucket and keys.
setup.sendMail: Send mail through a mail server
setup.siteHint: Where your app runs: where a user lands after a sign-in or confirmation link.
setup.siteUrlBad: Site URL must start with http:// or https://.
setup.size: The first setup downloads about 670 MB of images (1.9 GB on disk), which takes a few minutes. Once started it uses about 170 MB of memory idle, and about 360 MB under load. Every key and password is made for this project alone and written to {folder}{sep}.env.
